A.explanation: This is about half the required value, obtained if the sphere radius $1.2\text{ cm}$ is confused with the diameter when finding a moment arm.

B.explanation: Taking moments about the table edge gives $W_{sphere} \times 1.2\text{ cm} = 0.43\text{ N} \times 3.6\text{ cm}$, giving $m \approx 0.13\text{ kg}$.

C.explanation: This assumes the pivot is at the right-hand end of the $12\text{ cm}$ box, giving arms $6.0\text{ cm}$ and $1.2\text{ cm}$ and ignoring that the pivot is $2.4\text{ cm}$ from that end.

D.explanation: This is the sphere weight in newtons, about $1.3\text{ N}$, with division by $g$ omitted so force is misread as mass.

hints: Notice where the table edge touches the box in the diagram: it is under the left-hand side of the $2.4\text{ cm}$ sphere, so the pivot is $2.4\text{ cm}$ left of the right-hand end of the $12\text{ cm}$ box.
Find each perpendicular distance from that pivot: the box centre is $6.0\text{ cm}$ from its end, and the uniform sphere centre is one radius $1.2\text{ cm}$ from its end.
Set clockwise moment equal to anticlockwise moment about the pivot, solve for the sphere weight, then use $m = W/g$ with $g = 9.81\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
walkthrough: Identify the pivot and the two weights. The pivot is the table edge, which is $2.4\text{ cm}$ left of the right end of the box because it lines up with the left side of the touching $2.4\text{ cm}$ sphere.
Locate the lines of action. The box weight $0.43\text{ N}$ acts at its geometric centre, $6.0\text{ cm}$ from the right end, so its distance left of the pivot is $6.0 - 2.4 = 3.6\text{ cm}$.
Locate the sphere weight. Its centre is one radius from the end it touches, so $1.2\text{ cm}$ left of the right end. Its distance right of the pivot is $2.4 - 1.2 = 1.2\text{ cm}$.
Apply the principle of moments for equilibrium about the pivot: sum of clockwise moments equals sum of anticlockwise moments. Hence $W_s \times 1.2\text{ cm} = 0.43\text{ N} \times 3.6\text{ cm}$.
Solve: $W_s = 0.43 \times 3.6 / 1.2 = 1.29\text{ N}$. Convert to mass: $m = W_s/g = 1.29/9.81 \approx 0.13\text{ kg}$. This is option B.
